title: The Blue door of the shed
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：blue　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 blue 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the doctor wrote of ① a blue door of the shed in the chart, and everybody in the clinic said at once that it was ② bluer than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the doctor, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the blue ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the bluest door of the shed anybody in the clinic had ever seen, or so the chart for January 1946 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too blue to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the patient who had come to help; the blue ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the bandage at the far bed, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a blue mood on Sunday, and said that no patient in his right mind would call it ⑥ as blue as the mood on Sunday they had once had in the old clinic. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was blue or not, and he said so.

By 1959 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the chart. What the line asked for was ⑦ something blue, and nothing besides. The patient from the next clinic called the whole plan ⑧ quite blue; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the chart kept the names of the blue ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1962, for the whole place, she wrote of another blue door of the shed in the same chart, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ bluer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The bluest mood on Sunday in the whole clinic, she said in 1964, was the one she could never quite name; the blue ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 蓝色（前置定语 a blue door of the shed：1952 年大夫在病历里记下的那件蓝色的门）
B. adj. 蓝色／忧郁（比较级 bluer than：文中两处，一处比棚屋的门，一处比预想）
C. adj. 蓝色／忧郁（最高级 the bluest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 蓝色（表语 too blue to do：母亲觉得它太蓝色，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 忧郁（前置定语 a blue mood on Sunday：叔叔把整件事称作一桩忧郁的低落）
F. adj. 忧郁（同级比较 as blue as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩周日的低落相比）
G. adj. 忧郁（后置定语 something blue：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 忧郁（受程度副词修饰 quite blue：那位病人的评价）

items.q: a blue door of the shed
the bluest door of the shed anybody
The bluest mood on Sunday in

answers.why: blue 意为“蓝色”，1952 年大夫在病历里记下的是“一件蓝色的门”，此处作前置定语 a blue door of the shed。
blue 意为“蓝色”，此处用比较级 bluer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
blue 意为“蓝色”，病历上 一月 那行字说它是卫生所里最蓝色的一件，故用最高级 the bluest door of the shed。
blue 意为“蓝色”，母亲认为这件东西“太蓝色了，谁也用不上”，too blue to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
blue 意为“忧郁”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩忧郁的低落”，此处作前置定语 a blue mood on Sunday。
blue 意为“忧郁”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩周日的低落一样忧郁”，同级比较用 as blue as。
blue 意为“忧郁”，病历上那半行字要的是“忧郁的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something blue。
blue 意为“忧郁”，邻卫生所来的那位病人认为这套计划“相当忧郁”，quite 修饰原级 blue。
blue 意为“忧郁”，1962 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要忧郁”，故用比较级 bluer than。
blue 意为“忧郁”，母亲 1964 年说的是“整个卫生所里最忧郁的那一桩”，故用最高级 the bluest mood on Sunday。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1952 年，大夫在病历里记下了一件蓝色的门。（a blue door of the shed）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更蓝色。（bluer than …）
母亲觉得它太蓝色，谁也用不上。（too blue to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩忧郁的低落。（a blue mood on Sunday）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩周日的低落一样忧郁。（as blue as …）
到了 1959 年，病历上只剩半行字：要的是一件忧郁的东西。（something blue）
answers: In 1952 the doctor wrote of a blue door of the shed in the chart.
Everybody said it was bluer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too blue to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a blue mood on Sunday.
He said nobody would call it as blue as the mood on Sunday they had once had.
By 1959 the chart asked for nothing but something blue.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 blue 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1952 the doctor wrote of a blue door of the shed in the chart, and nobody forgot it.
It was the bluest door of the shed in the clinic, or so the chart says.
My mother thought it too blue to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a blue mood on Sunday, and nobody argued with him.
The patient from the next clinic called the plan quite blue, and everybody laughed.
The blue ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
